bibliographic.title: On the Complexities of Testing for Compliance with Human Oversight Requirements in AI Regulation
bibliographic.authors: Markus Langer; Veronika Lazar; Kevin Baum
bibliographic.citation_apa: Langer, M., Lazar, V., & Baum, K. (2026). On the complexities of testing for compliance with human oversight requirements in AI regulation. In B. Steffen (Ed.), AISoLA 2025 (LNCS 16220, pp. 160–169). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-07132-3_11

methodology.method_family: conceptual regulatory analysis and argumentative perspective
methodology.sector: AI regulation and high-risk AI systems
methodology.technology_context: AI-based systems for high-risk tasks; (semi-)autonomous agentic systems; compliance testing under emerging AI legislation including the European AI Act

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper directly addresses human oversight, compliance testing, auditing, and AI Act requirements in regulated high-risk AI contexts, which aligns with governance dimensions of the review. Provided text does not specifically address conversational AI, chatbots, agents in conversational settings, or LLM-based systems, so it is better classified as supporting rather than central evidence for conversational LLM governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python metadata incorrectly merged affiliation text into the title field; full-text coverage in the prompt is partial (pages 1-2, 4, 7 only), limiting appraisal completeness.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual perspective paper without empirical sample or reported primary data collection. Argumentative analysis is appropriate for identifying regulatory testing challenges but offers limited directly transferable operational guidance for conversational LLM systems.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is coherent and clearly linked to AI Act human oversight and compliance testing, but relevance to conversational LLM governance is indirect and the available excerpt set does not show empirical validation or LLM-specific operational mechanisms.

coding.theme: Challenges in testing compliance with human oversight requirements
coding.subtheme: Operationalizing AI Act Article 14 through auditing and empirical oversight evaluation

synthesis.main_claim: Testing compliance with human oversight requirements under the European AI Act is inherently complex because checklist-based approaches may be ineffective while empirical, context-sensitive testing is resource-intensive and difficult to standardize.
synthesis.contribution: The paper frames human oversight compliance as a sociotechnical governance challenge, identifies tensions between simple audits and empirical effectiveness testing, and argues for integrating psychology and HCI expertise into AI governance.
synthesis.limitations: Human oversight requirements are context-dependent, standards are difficult to operationalize, and transferring oversight effectiveness insights across contexts may be challenging.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on human oversight, compliance testing, and auditing challenges in regulated AI governance; not as primary evidence for conversational or LLM-specific governance mechanisms.
